findings.title: Negative slice start raises ValueError in Django — "advanced" negative-offset path always 500s
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`, where `start_offset = cursor.offset`). Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for any slice whose `start` or `stop` is negative, so this branch can never succeed. The inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong. Because `Endpoint.paginate` only converts `BadPaginationError` into a 400, this ValueError propagates and the request returns an unhandled HTTP 500 for any client-supplied cursor such as `?cursor=0:-5:0&optimized_pagination=true`. If negative offsets are meant to be rejected, they should raise `BadPaginationError`; if they are meant to be supported, they must be translated into a real positive offset/ordering flip.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is incompatible with the datetime ordering it is used with
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(value))`/`math.ceil(value)` on `getattr(item, self.key)` and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw `cursor.value`. The only caller (`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`) instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `value` is a `datetime`: `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`, which happens inside `build_cursor` on every request that takes this path. Additionally, when a cursor value is present, `build_queryset` will emit raw SQL comparing the `datetime` column to an integer (`"datetime" <= %s` with an int param), producing a database type error on Postgres. The optimized path therefore cannot work at all for this endpoint; it needs `DateTimePaginator`-style key conversion (multiplier + `datetime.fromtimestamp`) or must not be used with a datetime sort key.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` may be None, causing AttributeError/500
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` unconditionally. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional and is `None` for requests that are not made by an org member — e.g. org-level auth tokens / integration tokens, or a superuser-style actor with no membership (in that case `request.user.is_superuser` is False for token auth because `request.user` is anonymous). The short-circuit does not protect those cases, so the expression raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` and the audit log endpoint returns a 500 instead of the normal paginated response. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None and ...`.

findings.title: Privilege gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` and `has_global_access`, so it is not an admin-only gate
findings.body: The new branch is gated on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, and the comments describe it as "for authorized administrators" that "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Two problems: (1) Sentry's convention is `is_active_superuser(request)` — reading `user.is_superuser` directly ignores the superuser session/elevated-privilege requirement, so a superuser account without an active superuser session (and without the usual staff checks) passes the check; (2) `has_global_access` is true for ordinary members of organizations with open membership, so effectively any regular member can toggle the alternative code path by adding `?optimized_pagination=true`. The gate therefore does not restrict the behavior to administrators as the comment claims. The toggle is also an undocumented, unvalidated query parameter (it is not part of `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`) rather than a feature flag/option, so there is no way to turn it off operationally.

findings.title: BasePaginator offset clamping is inconsistent and leaves the is_prev crash in place
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behavior for every endpoint that uses `BasePaginator`. For forward cursors a client-supplied negative offset is now silently clamped to 0 (returning page-one rows instead of surfacing an error for a malformed cursor), while for `is_prev` cursors the negative value is still passed straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, where Django raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` and the request 500s. The accompanying comment ("This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is incorrect — the queryset rejects negative slices. Either validate the offset once and raise `BadPaginationError` (yielding a 400), or clamp in both branches; note also that the subsequent `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the unclamped `offset`, so the two values can disagree.

findings.title: Comment documents negative cursor offsets as a supported optimization, which is false
findings.body: The added comment on `Cursor.__init__` claims negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization" enabling "efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions". No validation was added or removed here, and negative offsets are not supported anywhere downstream: Django refuses negative slice starts (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`) and the offset-based paginators explicitly raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. Leaving this comment in a shared utility invites future callers to construct negative-offset cursors that will crash at query time; either remove the comment or add an explicit validation/rejection of negative offsets here.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: A new public paginator class (`OptimizedCursorPaginator`) and a new request-driven branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` are introduced without any tests. The behaviors that most need coverage are exactly those that are currently broken: a negative `cursor` offset with `optimized_pagination=true`, pagination with the `-datetime` sort key (which raises `TypeError` in `get_item_key`), and the permission gate when `organization_context.member` is `None`. Without tests these regressions reach production as 500s on a customer-facing endpoint.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and will drift
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` with one branch added, and it dropped the explanatory comments about the extra fetched row and the `post_query_filter` semantics. Any future fix to the base implementation (for example the offset clamping just added, or the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` off-by-one when offset is clamped) has to be applied in two places and will silently diverge here. Override only the slicing step (e.g. a `_slice_bounds` hook) instead of copying the whole method.
